chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who performs salat (prayer) between graves. He said: “That is not جائز except if he places between himself and the graves, when he performs salat (prayer), ten cubits in front of him, ten cubits behind him, ten cubits on his right, and ten cubits on his left; then he may perform salat (prayer), if he wishes.”

key_terms.الْقُبُورِ: the graves; burial places near which the ruling applies
key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ: in front of him; the forward direction in measuring distance
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَذْرُعٍ: ten cubits; the required measured distance
key_terms.عَنْ يَسَارِهِ: on his left; the left-side direction in measuring distance
key_terms.عَنْ يَمِينِهِ: on his right; the right-side direction in measuring distance
key_terms.لَا يَجُوزُ: it is not permissible; indicates legal prohibition or non-validity in context
key_terms.مِنْ خَلْفِهِ: behind him; the rear direction in measuring distance

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) between graves in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding performing salat (prayer) in an area between graves. It states that such salat (prayer) is not permitted unless a distance of ten cubits is maintained from the graves in all four directions around the person praying.
